mundari_locator_ready_statements.locator: Language Atlas of India 1991, Non-Scheduled Languages section, Mundari analytical note
mundari_locator_ready_statements.content_summary: The Atlas reports 861,378 Mundari speakers in the 1991 Census, 0.10 percent of the population excluding Jammu & Kashmir, with principal concentrations in Bihar and Orissa and district-level distributions.
mundari_locator_ready_statements.promotion_state: locator-ready; not promoted to controlled evidence in this run
mundari_locator_ready_statements.reason_not_promoted: Exact printed page/map number and immutable lawful binary SHA-256 were not established in this run.

mundari_locator_ready_statements.content_summary: The Atlas separately reports Munda as an Austric language and discusses its speaker distribution; this must not be silently merged with the Mundari census category.
mundari_locator_ready_statements.promotion_state: locator-ready; not promoted to controlled evidence in this run

canonicalization.rule: PARI PDF/page, library catalogue records, Census references and search snippets are manifestations or metadata records for one underlying 2004 Census publication, not independent corroborating sources.
canonicalization.dependency_rule: Later works quoting the 1991 Atlas remain dependent on the Census source for those statistics.

rights_access_governance.cultural_uncertainty_note: Census language labels and enumerated categories are administrative/statistical categories; they are not treated as community validation of linguistic identity or equivalence.

blocked_and_continued.action: Logged block; continued verification using PARI descriptive record, CiNii, NDL and official Census material.
